findings.title: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process is always False for spawn processes, so hung/dead flusher processes are never killed
findings.body: The flusher explicitly creates processes with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"), so the objects are SpawnProcess instances. However, `multiprocessing.Process` resolves to the *default* context's class (ForkProcess on Linux), and SpawnProcess does not subclass it. Therefore `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` in `_ensure_processes_alive` (line 254) and in `join` (line 346) evaluates to False for every flusher process, and `process.kill()` / `process.terminate()` are silently never executed. Consequences: when a flusher process hangs, `_ensure_processes_alive` spawns a replacement without killing the hung one, leaving two processes flushing the same shards and producing duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic; and on shutdown, processes are never terminated and linger as (daemon) zombies until interpreter exit. The old single-process code had the same latent isinstance bug in `join`, but the new restart path makes it load-bearing. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or just call kill/terminate unconditionally, or track which entries are threads vs processes).

findings.title: join() breaks out of the process-wait loop on deadline, skipping terminate() for all remaining processes
findings.body: In `join`, if the deadline is exhausted while waiting for one process, the `break` exits the for-loop over `self.processes` entirely, so none of the remaining processes get `process.terminate()` called (the terminate happens per-iteration after the wait). Previously there was only one process so this couldn't happen. With multiple flusher processes, a slow-to-stop process causes all later processes to be left running after join returns. The terminate should be applied to every remaining process even after the deadline, or the loop should continue with zero remaining time so terminate still runs.

findings.title: Restart limit check allows MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS + 1 restarts per process
findings.body: `if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` is checked before incrementing, so the RuntimeError only fires on the 12th unhealthy detection (restarts 0..10 are permitted, i.e. 11 restarts) even though the constant is named MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS = 10. This was inherited from the previous single-process code but is now duplicated per process; with N processes the consumer tolerates 11*N restarts before crashing. Use `>=` to match the constant's intent.

findings.title: Default --flusher-processes=1 contradicts the stated goal of one flusher process per shard
findings.body: The new CLI option defaults to 1, meaning a default deployment of process-spans gets a single flusher process shared across all shards via `flusher_processes` being passed to SpanFlusher. But the PR description says the intent is to "spawn a process per redis shard", and SpanFlusher's own default when max_processes is None is `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (one process per shard). Because the click default (1) is always passed, the SpanFlusher default is effectively unreachable from the CLI. If per-shard processes are the intended default, the click default should be None (or omitted) so SpanFlusher falls back to one process per shard.
